title: Acute Bacterial Meningitis in Adults – A Review of 493 Episodes

claims.text: In community-acquired adult bacterial meningitis, the most common organisms were Streptococcus pneumoniae (37%), Neisseria meningitidis (13%), and Listeria monocytogenes (10%).
claims.byte_quote: Streptococcus pneumoniae (37 percent), Neisseria meningitidis (13 percent), and Listeria monocytogenes (10 percent)

claims.text: Gram-negative bacilli (other than Haemophilus influenzae) caused 33% of nosocomial episodes but only 3% of community-acquired episodes.
claims.byte_quote: Gram-negative bacilli (other than Haemophilus influenzae) caused 33 percent of the nosocomial episodes but only 3 percent of the community-acquired episodes

claims.text: Only 19 of the 493 meningitis episodes (4%) were due to H. influenzae.
claims.byte_quote: Only 19 of the 493 episodes of meningitis (4 percent) were due to H. influenzae

claims.text: S. pneumoniae, N. meningitidis, and L. monocytogenes together accounted for only 8% of the nosocomial episodes.
